- Three web frameworks are cleanly separated (django.ts, fastapi.ts, flask.ts) without cross-contamination, enabling independent framework evolution
- Client analysis (HTTP, gRPC, queue) integrates with Python symbol rules through framework pack interface without tight coupling
- Perfect cohesion (1.0) with zero coupling demonstrates complete isolation from other language packs and runtime
- "packages/lang-python/src/index.ts" is production code imported only by tests (2 importer(s), all test files) — either it is dead or its real caller is missing
- The index.ts / pack.ts split is the documented contract: pack.ts builds the LanguagePackEntry that sourcevision loads dynamically, and index.ts is the single public entry that also re-exports internals for corpus scripts and tests. go-language-pack and java-language-pack use the same layout.
- The existing finding that packages/lang-python/src/index.ts is imported only by tests is a false positive. The package is loaded, never imported: sourcevision's pack-loader imports it dynamically at run time, which the static import graph cannot see. The dead-code heuristic should exempt the entry modules of runtime-loaded packs (lang-*/src/index.ts, pack.ts) so it stops recommending deletion of the public entry.
- lang-python splits detection by framework into one module each (django.ts, fastapi.ts, flask.ts). The Go and Java packs split by concern instead (pack, resolver, sql). Pack internal layout has no documented convention.
- Document the internal layout a pack should follow in lang-kit's AGENTS.md next to the pack contract: <lang>-pack.ts as the entry, <lang>-resolver.ts for imports, and one module per framework. New packs would then follow a single shape, and the 13 entry points in lang-python could be reached through one index.ts.
